newsitem.title: USA: Racist hotline alarms St. Louis area.
newsitem.headline: Racist hotline alarms St. Louis area.

text.p: Authorities Tuesday were investigating who was behind a telephone "hotline" that urged callers to identify blacks they wanted killed and offer reasons why.

Scores of people across the Mississippi River in St. Louis were contacted on their telephone pagers to call the number and were greeted with a hate-filled tape-recorded message saying killing blacks was "really fun."

Rev. Johnnie Scott, head of the local office of the National Association for the Advancement of Coloured People, notified East St. Louis police and prosecutors that several workers in his office were paged.
The message asked callers to leave the name of a black person they wanted killed, and the reason.
"It isn't funny," Scott said. "We don't want to encourage people to do this. We have enough sick people on the street who would want to carry out this act."
